# U02 synthetic contract fixtures

Everything under `package/` is test-only, including the eight `SYNTHETIC-SYS-*`
IDs, source bytes, review question, instruction/reference metadata and claimed
synthetic observations. No live company source was read and no human approval or
request delivery occurred. Production code has no fixture-selection path.

The seven snapshots form an exact-byte chain. The hidden `.completion.json`
binds its current run and Stage 07 bytes. `analysis/request.json` and
`analysis/response.json` exercise the skill/Python packet shape without a model
call. Null host/model/effort/usage values describe unknown provider metadata.

The three artifact files are deliberately plain synthetic byte payloads. Their
contract `valid` state means the synthetic byte bindings match; they do not
establish CSV/brief/iCalendar grammar or acceptance. U14–U17 own real artifact
format/meaning checks. U02 tests construct minimal empty/blocked variants and
violations in isolated temporary copies; no test rewrites these fixtures.

Review regressions also build a retained one-pixel PNG and separate synthetic
derived UTF-8 text in temporary copies. They demonstrate acquisition/derivation
lineage and packet bindings, without claiming meaningful OCR was performed.
Multi-basis actions retain separate synthetic policy and legal impact records.
Feedback regressions build a separate prior run under a temporary `history/`
root, with actual request/artifact byte bindings and an explicit current-run
revalidation report. Claimed historical identifiers and hashes remain unchanged.
Unmatchable feedback remains unresolved. Policy-control regressions use fresh
run/snapshot/record identities while checking stable business IDs and calendar
UIDs for unchanged meaning. No human authority or real applicability is claimed.
